query: p-queue 的 strict 模式与默认的固定窗口限流相比，在窗口边界附近的任务突发行为上有什么不同？

relevant_passages.anchor: - **Default mode (fixed window)**: Tasks can burst at window boundaries. You could execute 2 tasks at 999ms and 2 more at 1000ms, resulting in 4 tasks within 1ms.

distractor_passages.anchor: - You're interacting with APIs that enforce strict rate limits and will throttle or block you if you exceed them, even briefly

rationale: The strict-mode option block contrasts fixed-window bursts with a sliding window that caps runs in any rolling interval, whereas the FAQ entry only advises when strict mode is worth its extra overhead and never describes boundary bursting.

query: If a task waits in the p-queue backlog before it is allowed to run, does its configured timeout already count that waiting time?

relevant_passages.anchor: The timeout begins when the operation is dequeued and starts execution, not while it's waiting in the queue.

distractor_passages.anchor: You can set a timeout for all tasks or override it per task. When a task times out, a `TimeoutError` is thrown.

rationale: The option reference states that the clock starts only when the operation is dequeued and begins execution, while the timeout how-to only shows how to set global and per-task limits and never says when the clock starts.

query: How can I keep p-timeout's deadline working when a test installs sinon's fake timers?

relevant_passages.anchor: Useful for testing purposes, in particular to work around [`sinon.useFakeTimers()`](https://sinonjs.org/releases/latest/fake-timers/).

distractor_passages.anchor: The package uses `setTimeout` and `clearTimeout` from the global scope, so you can use the [Node.js test timer mocking](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html#class-mocktimers) or a package like [`sinon`](https://github.com/sinonjs/sinon).

rationale: The customTimers option exists precisely to pass the real setTimeout and clearTimeout around sinon's fakes, whereas the p-retry FAQ only says that timers are taken from the global scope and mentions mocking libraries without offering an override.

query: Which rate-limit and server-side failure responses does the OpenAI Node client retry out of the box?

relevant_passages.anchor: 429 Rate Limit, and >=500 Internal errors will all be retried by default.

distractor_passages.anchor: Returns a `Promise` that is fulfilled when calling `input` returns a fulfilled promise. If calling `input` returns a rejected promise, `input` is called again until the max retries are reached, it then rejects with the last rejection reason.

rationale: The Retries section names 429 Rate Limit and >=500 Internal errors as automatically retried, whereas the p-retry reference describes its own promise-based retry loop and never names any OpenAI HTTP status.

query: In agentkeepalive, how can an error handler tell that an ECONNRESET happened on a reused keep-alive socket so that a retry is justified?

relevant_passages.anchor: This agent implements the `req.reusedSocket` to determine whether a request is send through a reused socket.

rationale: The reusedSocket section exposes a per-request flag that marks a socket as reused for exactly this ECONNRESET retry decision, while the usage example only shows how to construct an agent with socket limits and never mentions reusedSocket.

query: I give an OpenAI request a 20-second timeout and also wrap the call in p-retry with maxRetryTime: does the SDK itself retry requests that time out, and which clock does p-retry use to enforce that overall deadline?

relevant_passages.anchor: Note that requests which time out will be [retried twice by default](#retries).
Measured with a monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) so system clock adjustments do not affect the limit.

rationale: The OpenAI timeout section says a timed-out request is retried twice by default, so the combined retry budget must account for both layers, and the p-retry maxRetryTime option states that the overall deadline is measured with a monotonic performance.now() clock immune to system clock changes.
